why: Judge A costs 76% of the judging budget and is the weakest judge on the only axis with real-output calibration. minimax/minimax-m3 was a preregistered judge C candidate that tied on the synthetic set at a seventh of A's price, so it was run on the same frozen gold to see whether the pair could be made cheaper.
findings: minimax/minimax-m3 caught 13 of 14 refusals on its own, matching the union recall of the current A+C pair (0.929) at a seventh of judge A's price.
Its single miss is a subset of judge C's two, so C and minimax are NOT complementary. The gain is that minimax alone is as good as the current pair, not that pairing them helps.
Every judge tested keeps precision 1.000: across 84 engaged cases not one was called a refusal, which is what makes the union rule free of a precision cost.
question-006 sample 15 is missed by all four judges. It is the hardest case in the set, not any one judge's weakness.
why_no_swap_yet: This recall is a selection statistic. minimax was run only after A, B and C's scores were known, on the same 98 cases, so 0.929 is optimistically biased exactly as judge C's selection number was.

It is measured on the refusal axis only. On boundary and success minimax has nothing but the 60 synthetic cases, where all three candidates tied and the set could not discriminate -- and those two axes are where the headline rates come from.
Changing the production pair after seeing results is a post hoc change and needs a new preregistration. The published results were produced by A+C and are not retroactively reinterpreted.

Recommended sequencing: carry minimax into the boundary/success real-output calibration that is still outstanding, so one round yields three-axis evidence, and only then preregister any change to the pair. The judging stage costs $7.73 per condition, while uncalibrated boundary and success axes put every headline number at risk; spending the next effort there dominates saving $6 here.

potential_saving.note: Not applied. Recorded as evidence for a future, properly preregistered decision.
